messages:
mira: Hey team — customer reporting repeated streaming cutoffs around ~60s for the generation endpoint. They included a curl and a request id: r-0a1b2c3d4e. Said it happens behind their corp proxy and only for certain regions (us-west2). Can someone help validate the curl repro and auth headers?

dan: I can take a look. Quick Q: are they using token rotation or short-lived creds?

mira: They said they rotate tokens every 45s in their client, but the server shows the request accepted with the original token. Might be client dropping connection during refresh.

alex: Can you paste the exact curl they used? Also ask them to run with --trace-time to capture timings.

mira: Pasting the curl they sent: ```
curl -v --http2 -N \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Client-Version: customer-app/1.2.3" \
  --data '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"stream test"}' \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate/stream"
```

dan: OK. A few things to verify: 1) they should send a persistent connection (keepalive) and not re-issue curl per chunk. 2) check for `Expect: 100-continue` oddities. 3) proxy often injects buffering — ask for `curl --raw` and `-o /dev/null --dump-header -` outputs.

alex: Also confirm they include `-N` (no-buffer) and not `--compressed` (some proxies buffer compressed responses). Suggest adding `--no-buffer` in some curl versions.

mira: I asked them to run this variant and include trace: ```
curl -vvv --http2 -N --no-buffer --trace-time --trace-ascii /tmp/curl.trace \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"stream test"}' \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate/stream"
```

sre-bot: note: when you paste traces please redact full bearer tokens and internal IPs. keep the request-id header if present.

lee-cs: Customer ran it and attached trace (redacted). They see first 60s of chunks then connection abruptly closed by their proxy with FIN from 10.8.0.1. They also provided server logs snippet: 

```
[2026-02-17T18:02:03Z] INFO request_id=r-0a1b2c3d4e start stream client=10.8.32.12 region=us-west2 model=redwood-1
[2026-02-17T18:03:04Z] WARN request_id=r-0a1b2c3d4e upstream closed by client after 61s
[2026-02-17T18:03:04Z] INFO request_id=r-0a1b2c3d4e tokens_emitted=312
```

dan: That lines up with a proxy idle timeout ~60s. Two options: 1) client sends periodic keepalive pings (we stream a zero-length chunk or ":keepalive" event) 2) route through a proxy that preserves long-lived SSE/HTTP2 streams.

alex: From our side we should validate server-side: check nginx/X-frontend keepalive settings and ensure no proxy-level timeouts are cutting the TCP. Also check our LB's idle timeout for that customer region.

mira: Customer also asked if authorization rotation could cause server to close mid-stream. From logs it accepted the token and continued — so unlikely. But they should confirm they are not reissuing a new TCP connection while rotating token.

lee-cs: They can share a debug bundle. What exact pieces do you want?

dan: Ask for: 1) curl.trace (from --trace-time), 2) full curl command they used, 3) tcpdump (pcap) around the failure window, 4) client logs showing token rotation, 5) server request logs we can match by request_id. If possible, a small HAR of the request.

alex: Also request the `x-request-id` response header and any `traceparent` values. We can correlate with our distributed traces.

mira: I'll send a checklist to the customer and ask them to run the enhanced curl and collect pcap. Also suggested a quick workaround: add a periodic NOP chunk every 30s to keep proxies happy.

sre-bot: Recommended diagnostic commands to include in the bundle:
```
# curl with trace
curl -vvv --http2 -N --no-buffer --trace-time --trace-ascii /tmp/curl.trace \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"stream test"}' \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate/stream"
# tcpdump example (run with sudo)
sudo tcpdump -i any -w /tmp/stream-fail.pcap host api.redwood.example and port 443 and (tcp[((tcp[12:1] & 0xf0) >> 2):1] != 0)
```

lee-cs: Customer replied they'll collect and send a bundle with redacted token and the server log tail. ETA ~2 hours. :thumbsup:

mira: Thanks all — I'll attach the bundle here when it arrives and we'll triage correlation with our traces (request_id r-0a1b2c3d4e). If we need to hotfix the LB idle thresholds we'll loop infra.

alex: if we confirm proxy timeout, we should add a note to the docs about keepalive recommendations for streaming customers.

mira: good call. Closing for now, will re-open thread when bundle lands. :white_check_mark:
